title: Props, every state
prompt: Paint one sheet of cut-out puppet parts for a paper-puppet film, using the attached image. Panel A is the exact layout, panel B is our footage for these props (reference: copy the object, not the photo style), panel C is the style. STYLE (panel C): flat cards cut from corrugated cardboard, gouache with confident ink linework, the flutes faintly showing through the paint, a thin raw kraft-brown cut edge round every card, brass split-pin brads; shot flat-on, even light, no shadows, no perspective. Copy the craft from C, not the clothes in it. WHAT (panel B): the props of the poem 'New Day', one row each, every state of a prop in its own cell, left to right: the new temple: a futuristic, modern, clean white temple: a three-course platform, six columns, seven entablature blocks, two pediment slopes and one finial; chalk white, crisp edges, no ornament (site (rubble only), courses laid, columns and beams, complete, silhouette at blue hour, lit by the sun); the finial: a short white spire on the pediment apex whose tip carries the poem's one accent. No still fits. (arriving, complete, tip lit); the chapel ruin and rubble: roofless rust-grey stone walls, one arch, fallen stones wet with dew that dries in the sun (wet, dark, dew drying in sun, under the new platform); the journal: a worn leather-bound journal with handwritten pages, stored away for moments of clarity. No still fits. (under the arm, opened, read aloud, closed); the sun over the ridge: gold disc drawn only where it has cleared the hills. No still fits. (under the hills, clearing the ridge, up with rays); the parked motorcycle: the bike from 10, parked by the ruin. No still fits. (parked). Paint each state as a flat cardboard prop card at the size its cell gives, the same object across its row; a brass brad on the green cross (its pivot); where there is a red cross, that is where a hand grips it. LAYOUT (panel A): paint one card inside each grey ghost, in the same place, size and angle, inside its dashed outline; a brass brad exactly on every green cross; each red cross must fall inside that card's rounded end. NEVER draw a pelvis, hip, shorts or briefs card (the thighs end in a rounded seat that tucks under the hem), a sleeveless vest, lace-up boots, or sunglasses painted onto a head. OUTPUT: only the painted cards on a pure white 2048x1152 sheet laid out as panel A. Leave out panels B and C, the crosses, labels, ruler, dashed lines and ghosts.
